shifts.summary: The shift 1 paper was judged overall as Easy to Moderate, with candidates reporting they attempted about 69–79 questions well. Timing was tight, especially for reasoning and quantitative sections, and a system freeze lasted about 10‑11 minutes. Math questions were longer than usual, while English comprehension was manageable for fast readers.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Timing was tight; only about 16‑17 reasoning questions could be attempted.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Math questions took extra time due to length. Each shift had ~15 easy, 5‑6 moderate, 3‑4 tough questions; decimal/approximation questions appear 3‑4 per shift.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: Fast readers could finish English quickly.

asked.q: Long math questions with four‑line statements
Reasoning questions were mostly correct but limited by time
Value of tanθ + cotθ when θ = 45°
Compute a² + b² given a = 4, b = 7
Volume of a rectangular pyramid with base l=4, b=6, height = 5/2
Volume of a triangular prism with given side lengths
Work problem: A finishes work in 8 days, B in 12 days, both work together for 3 days; find remaining work

observations: Timing was the biggest issue, especially for reasoning and math.
A system glitch froze the computer for about 10‑11 minutes.
Math questions were longer than usual, affecting speed.
disagreements: One report called overall difficulty Moderate, another Easy to Moderate.

intro: The SSC CGL Tier 1 exam was conducted on 12 October 2026 across three shifts. Shift 1 has a partial analysis indicating an overall difficulty ranging from easy to moderate, with candidates reporting successful attempts on roughly 69–79 questions. Shifts 2 and 3 are still pending and no usable analysis is available yet. All figures mentioned are unofficial, and SSC normalises scores across shifts for final ranking.
